# Agent experience (AX)

Guide for coding agents working on or with `@grok/agent-sdk`.
Loop: edit files → inspect surface → run a turn → assert with filesystem
evals. Prefer the CLI over ad-hoc curl.

User-facing documentation lives in [`docs/`](./docs/README.md)
(quickstart, concepts, guides, evals/hillclimbing, deployment,
troubleshooting, reference). This file is the terse loop reference;
point humans at the docs.

Start machine-readable docs at `dist/docs/llms.txt` when it exists, or at
`/docs/llms.txt` on a running host. Use `llms-full.txt` only when the whole
documentation set is needed.

Run the CLI under **Node, never Bun** — use the installed `bdk`
bin; from a source checkout of this package,
`pnpm exec tsx src/bin/agent-serve.ts <command> …` is equivalent. Bun's
HTTP/2 client corrupts local harness
tool-result streams (`NGHTTP2_FRAME_SIZE_ERROR`), which makes every
built-in read/grep fail and sends models into retry loops.

## Skills

Before scaffolding, wiring channels, writing evals, or deploying, **read the
matching skill under `skills/<task>/SKILL.md`** (paths
below are relative to this package). Those files ship with `@grok/agent-sdk`.
Cloud agents get the same published skills via `GetManagedSkills`,
which reads these files. Open them directly. Authoring notes live in
`skills/`, not in a second stub copy.

| Skill | Read it when |
| --- | --- |
| `skills/cli/SKILL.md` | Before any `bdk` command: `--json`, exit codes, `--fields`, `--dry-run`, `--yes`, secrets, untrusted output |
| `skills/framework-map/SKILL.md` | First contact: folder structure, runtime, sessions, state, invariants |
| `skills/create-agent/SKILL.md` | Scaffolding a new agent (interview → scaffold → verify) |
| `skills/evals/SKILL.md` | Writing evals; fixture strategy; the regression ratchet |
| `skills/otel/SKILL.md` | OpenTelemetry export (`OTEL_*` variables and `@opentelemetry/api`) |
| `skills/hillclimb/SKILL.md` | Improving an existing agent measurably |
| `skills/github/SKILL.md` | GitHub webhook agents; replay / forward / fixtures / cursor-events |
| `skills/setup-slack/SKILL.md` | Slack wiring and channel watching |
| `skills/mcp-auth/SKILL.md` | Host MCP OAuth (`mcp oauth`, `advertiseTools`, `host-connections/`, hosted `cursorAccount`) |
| `skills/deploy/SKILL.md` | Deploy or redeploy from a pushed Git ref with an attached service account |
| `skills/debug/SKILL.md` | Something misbehaving locally (symptom → cause) |

## Recommended loop

```bash
# 1. Discover / validate
agent-sdk validate --dir .
agent-sdk info --dir . --json

# One-shot turn (ephemeral server, JSON trajectory + single NDJSON trace)
agent-sdk run --dir . --message "What's the temperature in NYC?" --json
# → trace at <dir>/.agent-serve/traces/<sessionId>.ndjson
# Visualize: agent-sdk serve --dir .  then playground → Open trace

# Against a running server (deep-linkable in the playground)
agent-sdk serve --dir . &
agent-sdk run --url http://127.0.0.1:3000 --message "..." --json
# → JSON includes playgroundUrl?sessionId=...

# Optional: custom path / offline summary
agent-sdk run --dir . --message "..." --trace /tmp/run.ndjson
agent-sdk session get --file /tmp/run.ndjson

# Deterministic tool call (no model turn, no API key needed)
agent-sdk tool call get_weather --dir . --input '{"city":"NYC"}' --json
# → POST /v1/tools/get_weather; validates input, runs execute in-process

# 3. Evals (defineEval under evals/)
agent-sdk eval --dir . --list
agent-sdk eval --dir . --json
agent-sdk eval --dir . weather/nyc
```

## Project layout

```
my-agent/
  bot/
    agent.ts
    instructions.md
    tools/*.ts
    skills/*.md
    channels/
    ...
  evals/
    smoke.eval.ts            # single datapoint → id: smoke
    weather.eval.ts          # cases → weather/nyc, weather/paris, …
    evals.config.ts          # required: maxConcurrency; optional maxPlaygroundRuns (default 20)
```

## Authoring evals

```ts
import { defineEval, includes } from "@grok/agent-sdk/evals";

// One datapoint per file, or many via `cases` (ids = <fileId>/<case.id>)
export default defineEval({
  tags: ["smoke", "weather"],
  cases: [
    {
      id: "nyc",
      description: "Weather tool is used for temperature questions.",
      async test(t) {
        await t.send("What's the temperature in NYC?");
        t.succeeded();
        t.calledTool("get_weather");
        t.check(t.reply, includes(/°|[FC]/));
      },
    },
  ],
});
```

Select with the CLI: one datapoint (`weather/nyc`), a whole file
(`weather`), several ids, or omit for all.

`evals/evals.config.ts` must set `maxConcurrency` (hard-capped at 200 due to
model provider request limits; examples use `20`). Playground batches stay
in memory only (`maxPlaygroundRuns`, default 20), and a serve restart loses
them:

```ts
import { defineEvalConfig } from "@grok/agent-sdk/evals";

export default defineEvalConfig({
  maxConcurrency: 20,
});
```
## CLI notes for agents

The guardrails for running `bdk` from an agent are in `skills/cli/SKILL.md`.

- Output is text by default, also when piped. Pass `--json` for one JSON
  document on stdout; errors then print as `{"error":{"code","message","hint"}}`
  and the exit code names the failure (`agent-sdk help` lists the exit codes).
- `run` / `eval` start an ephemeral server on port 0 with a temp `stateRoot`
  outside the monorepo so session workspaces do not inherit ambient `AGENTS.md`.
- Point `--url` at an already-running agent to skip local host startup.
- `tool call <tool> --input '{...}'` invokes a server tool deterministically
  (schema-validated, in-process, no model). `--session <id>` runs it inside
  an existing session and records it on that session's event stream.
- `init` with no directory prints this setup guide (does not scaffold).
  `init <dir>` scaffolds (skipping existing files), runs `npm install`,
  offers to install/update package skills into
  `~/.cursor/skills/bdk/` (TTY only; always overwrites with the
  package copy, with `alwaysApply: true` so Cursor injects them).
  Consumer installs already copy those skills in postinstall; the
  source checkout does not. Links `bdk` onto the
  npm global bin (so bare `bdk` works on PATH), runs `login` and
  waits when unsigned, then prints `cd` (when needed) and `agent-sdk dev`.
  `--json` still installs but never blocks on login or skill install; it
  prints
  `{ ok, directory, created, skipped, installed, installError, cliOnPath, cliLinkError, next }`.
- `chat --json --message "..."` talks to a running server and prints a trajectory.

## Agent-to-agent (MCP endpoint + peer MCP connections)

Every mounted agent is also an MCP server at `/<slug>/v1/mcp` (streamable
HTTP, stateless, same auth chain as the session API). Tools: `ask`
(delegate a message; returns `{ status, sessionId, reply }`, with bounded
waits — `status: "running"` means keep waiting), `check` (wait/poll a
running session), and `call_tool` (deterministic server-tool passthrough,
only when the agent has server tools). Sessions created this way live on
the `mcp` channel and are visible in the playground.

Wire one agent to another with a **peer MCP connection**:

```ts
// bot/mcp-connections/weather.ts
export default defineConnection({ agent: "weather-agent" });
```

In a local multi-agent serve, peers resolve among the mounted agents. Unknown
slugs and self-references fail at startup. Cloud-runtime turns need
`--public-url` to reach the serve host.

A single-agent serve omits peers with a warning unless `peersUrl` /
`--peers-url` is set. A multi-agent serve rejects the option.

Cursor-managed hosting passes `--peers-url` automatically when the
installed CLI supports it. Team-owned deployments can reach declared peers
from the same team, whether the agents deploy together or separately. Only
the caller declares the relationship. Redeploy the caller after adding a
peer or when its current deployment predates hosted peer support.

There is no cross-host loop protection. Scope delegation in instructions so
A→B→A recursion cannot happen, such as a parent that delegates only weather
questions to a `weather-agent` peer.

```bash
agent-sdk dev ./agents
agent-sdk chat --url http://127.0.0.1:3000/concierge --message "Weather in Paris?"
```

## Slack channel

`slackChannel()` is a dedicated Socket Mode Slack app (no public Request
URL). Import from `@grok/agent-sdk/channels/slack`. Mint the app with
`agent-sdk slack create`; mention the bot (or DM it) in Slack.

```bash
agent-sdk slack setup
agent-sdk slack create --dir ./my-agent --channel-posts
# envPrefix from the directory name (MY_AGENT_SLACK_*)
# Manual path: agent-sdk slack init --manual --dir ./my-agent
agent-sdk slack doctor --prefix MY_AGENT
agent-sdk dev ./my-agent
```

Multi-agent serve needs **one Slack app (and token pair) per agent**:
`<PREFIX>_SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` + `<PREFIX>_SLACK_APP_TOKEN`. Missing tokens leave
that channel idle instead of failing `serve`. Single-agent setups can use the
shared `SLACK_*` vars (`slackChannel()` / `slack create --no-prefix`).

Channel watching is `engagement.channelPosts`.

Replies default to `reply: { mode: "post" }` (status chip while the turn
runs, one message at the end); `reply: { mode: "stream" }` streams the answer
with optional `toolCards` / `reasoningCard`. Suggested prompts default on.
Guided skill: `skills/setup-slack/SKILL.md`.

## Playground UI (Vite + React)

The web playground is a Vite + React SPA under `playground/` (entry
`playground/src/main.tsx`).

`agent-sdk serve` handles the Vite side for you:

- If `dist/playground/` is missing and the local vite toolchain is present,
  serve auto-runs `vite build` before listening.
- `serve --dev` / `dev` also starts Vite HMR (default `:5273`) and prints
  that URL as `playground`. Single-agent proxies `/v1` to the serve URL;
  multi-agent serves the agents index at `/` and each SPA at
  `/<slug>/playground` (pin one slug with `AGENT_SERVE_BASE=/<slug>`).

`pnpm run build` still emits the static bundle to `dist/playground/` (ships in
`dist/**`). Pure logic (markdown render, trace model) lives in
`playground/src/lib` with Vitest tests — prefer adding tests there.

## GitHub channel

Author `bot/channels/github.ts` with `githubChannel()` from
`@grok/agent-sdk/channels/github`; it mounts `POST /v1/channels/github`
and verifies `X-Hub-Signature-256` when a webhook secret is set. The channel
publishes the webhook events it dispatches on (derived from the declared hooks,
or pinned via `webhookEvents`) as `meta.githubWebhookEvents`. Auth default: with
a secret → `allowAll()` + signature check; without one → `localDevStrict()`,
except under `serve --dev` which admits unsigned loopback deliveries (so
`gh webhook forward` and fixtures work with no secret). Outbound GitHub API
calls can reuse the signed-in Cursor connection with
`githubChannel({ cursorAccount: { repos: ["owner/repo"] } })`; this supplies
events plus a refreshing repo-scoped credential to `ctx.github`,
`ctx.host.github`, and child `gh` commands in dev and hosted deployments.
Default `permissions: "pr-write"`; opt up to `"contents-write"` to push or
post merge-box checks. Enabling `progress.commitStatus` opts hosted
`cursorAccount` up to that tier (`checks:write`). Without `cursorAccount`, calls prefer
App installation tokens (`GITHUB_APP_ID` +
`GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` + webhook `installation.id` or
`GITHUB_APP_INSTALLATION_ID`); serve warmup also exports that token as
`GH_TOKEN` for tools that shell out to `gh`. For local testing, omit App
creds and use `GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GH_TOKEN` or `gh auth login`.

Test github agents against live deliveries with the CLI (wraps
`gh webhook forward`; URL + events auto-derived, repo inferred from the git
remote):

```bash
# one-time: gh + the cli/gh-webhook extension
agent-sdk github doctor --install

# what would be forwarded, per agent (URL + events)
agent-sdk github events --dir ./agents --json

# forward live deliveries to a served agent (no secret needed against --dev;
# set GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET to verify signatures)
agent-sdk dev ./my-agent &
agent-sdk github forward --dir ./my-agent
```

When several channels match (e.g. a folder of agent projects), one forwarder fans out to
all of them via a local proxy that re-posts each raw (still-signed) delivery to
the channels whose event set matches — `gh webhook forward` targets one URL and
GitHub allows only one forwarder per repo. `--repo` / `--org` override the
target, `--events` narrows the set, `--url` points at a tunnel, and `--slug` /
`--channel` forward to just one of several agents.

`gh webhook forward` requires **admin** on the repo (org owner for `--org`) and
authenticates its relay with the GitHub CLI's own login — so a `GITHUB_TOKEN` /
`GH_TOKEN` env override makes deliveries **401** (hook creation still succeeds,
which is the confusing part). Blank it for the command (`GITHUB_TOKEN= GH_TOKEN=
agent-sdk github forward …`) or `unset` it; `github doctor` / `forward` warn
when they detect an env token.

When you lack repo admin, or want deterministic runs (hillclimbing), use
`agent-sdk github replay <pr_url>` instead: it **reads** the PR via `gh api`
(pull access only, `GITHUB_TOKEN` is fine), synthesizes GitHub-shaped payloads,
signs them (`--secret`/`GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`), and POSTs them at the channel —
no admin, no relay. `--events` defaults to `pull_request` (`*` = the channel's
declared events); `--action`/`--conclusion`/`--comment`/`--context` tune each;
`--dry-run`/`--fixtures-dir DIR` print or snapshot payloads as fixtures.
Fixtures still work for offline replay: `POST` a saved payload with an
`x-github-event` header (no signature in `--dev`).

## Do not

- Proactively add or update documentation (`docs/`, READMEs, this file) as
  part of a code change. Docs are written intentionally, on explicit request
  only — never as a side effect of a feature or fix. If a change makes docs
  stale, say so in the PR description instead of editing them unprompted.
- Grow an agent's deterministic path by default. Host code owns side-effect
  gates and actuation, dedupe of external writes, auth, evidence seeding,
  and hard API caps; formatting, summarizing, classification, and reply
  composition stay with the model under an output contract in
  `instructions.md` / skills (prose in `.md`, never TS string builders).
  Speculative caches (prefetch, fingerprint dedupe, write coalescing) need
  measured pressure first, and framework gaps (posting, chunking, retries)
  get fixed or filed in the framework, not worked around in `bot/lib/`.
  Budget + smells: `skills/create-agent/SKILL.md` § "The deterministic-path
  budget".
- Nested git checkouts default `local.cwd` to `~/.cache/agent-serve/<dir>`.
  Point cwd at a checkout only when the agent must inherit that tree.
  `run` / `eval` already use a temp state root.
- Expect `bot/evals/` to be loaded — evals live at the **project root** `evals/`.
- Build optional object fields with a conditional empty-object spread.
  Assign the property directly; `undefined` is fine on optional keys.
  `bdk/no-conditional-empty-spread` enforces this.

  ```ts
  // ❌ BAD
  { ...(x === undefined ? {} : { x }) }
  { ...(cond && { x }) }

  // ✅ GOOD
  { x } // may be undefined
  ```

  Only use a conditional spread when merging a real partial object
  (`...overrides`), not to omit an optional key.
